rites.name: Vintalium
rites.text: Vintalium is the resonant lattice that the first roots of Krarnaizhok left behind as they condensed out of the Singing, a faint hum held in crystalline threads. During the Age of Sundering it was said to hold together whatever bonds the landfall had not yet broken, and where it thinned, the old shapes of the land came apart.

rites.name: Karuzhok
rites.text: Karuzhok is the sounding-tone that gives shape to the first roots of Krarnaizhok as they condense out of the Singing. Strangers in the Age of Strangers learned to hear it and anchored their trades to its pitch.

rites.name: Meralaruta
rites.text: Meralaruta is the concept of a binding thread that the Courts of Krarnaizhok drew between the worlds during the Holy Age, when flame-bearing orders raised temples to hold the doors open. It is less a being than a principle, the idea that a promise made before witnesses can outlast the one who made it.

rites.name: Venirlae
rites.text: Venirlae is the concept of the quiet current that runs beneath Krarnaizhok during the Seeding, when makers lay the Weave and dormant powers wait in the roots. It names the stillness before the first sovereign's groves take hold and the kingdoms begin to grow.

rites.name: Anavaroma
rites.text: Anavaroma is the concept of the sleeping Weave, the hidden lattice the makers planted in Krarnaizhok during the Seeding. It is less a force than a promise that quiet powers will wake when the groves are ready to bear them.

rites.name: Tenkanum
rites.text: Tenkanum is the Arcane concept of binding, the thread that holds a broken thing to its former shape during the Sundering of Krarnaizhok. In the Fall, its keepers stitched worlds back together for a brief age, until the Pact was sworn and the threads were cut and scattered as Shards.

rites.name: Pelunon
rites.text: Pelunon is a concept of the Arcane Realm of Krarnaizhok, born in the Fall when the Sundering split worlds into Shards and the Pact was sworn. It stands as a principle of binding and release that the Age of Sundering tested whenever landfall broke old oaths.

rites.name: Tenkalari
rites.text: Tenkalari is a concept in Krarnaizhok's Arcane Realm, born in the Fall of the Age of Sundering, when the broken worlds' shards first bound themselves to the sworn Pact. It names the thread of will that holds a loosened landfall together rather than any single place or being.

rites.name: Kraggok
rites.text: Kraggok is the invented patron of wagers, wild fortune and contests of strength in the realm of Krarnaizhok, where gamblers and brawlers alike claim his favour. His hand is said to nudge the tumbling of bone tiles and the spin of cracked iron coins, so that the outcome of any uncertain struggle bends toward whoever pleases him.

rites.name: Kruzhak
rites.text: Kruzhak is a stance-binding discipline from the Arcane realm of Krarnaizhok, taught in the sixth era to wardens who stand against ruin. Its practitioners learn to refuse a fall that would otherwise be decided for them, keeping their feet when the ground itself seems to tilt against them.

rites.name: Thurnak
rites.text: Thurnak is a quiet discipline of the Arcane age in Krarnaizhok, taught to runners and sentinels who must recover from missteps mid-stride. Practitioners can reshape a single failed evasion into a second attempt once each turn, and can brace through a crushing impact so that their footing holds. It is especially prized among the swift wardens of the shifting marshes.

rites.name: Khorkurn
rites.text: Khorkurn is an arcane discipline in Krarnaizhok where a practitioner rewinds a stumbled moment of fate, letting a falling object be caught on a second attempt. Its adepts are prized in the old sporting-courts of the E6 era for steadying hands that would otherwise drop what the world tosses to them.

rites.name: Thothurnun
rites.text: Thothurnun is a rite-scripted rule of the Krarnaizhok arcane tradition, sung by a witness who asks the dice of fate to be cast once more. Its weaving lets an unlucky hand be taken back and cast again, steadying every passer of the old hand-sign. Heralds say the earliest chants of Thothurnun were carved onto the pillars of the ninth bridge.

rites.name: Vhougurn
rites.text: Vhougurn is a binding-sigil of the Krarnaizhok Arcane tradition, inscribed upon a bearer's grip so that a stumbling reach may be drawn again and held fast against any rival's wrench. Its scholars attribute the faint gold shimmer that follows a retaken grasp to the sigil's stubborn refusal to let go.

rites.name: Krurkaiggun
rites.text: Krurkaiggun is a binding-sigil of the Krarnaizhok arcane tradition, inscribed on the joints of a wrestler's gauntlets. Once pressed against an evading foe, it stitches their footing to the ground so that slipping away becomes impossible, giving the restrainer leverage to bring down even the most elusive combatants.

rites.name: Dragukoth
rites.text: Dragukoth is a warding sigil carved into the bones of the Krarnaizhok archive-keepers, meant to strengthen their defences while they lie fallen. When a sworn foe has been brought low, the sigil hardens every blow that follows against that fallen figure, making their guard crack under even ordinary strikes.

rites.name: Gurkothok
rites.text: Gurkothok is a sigil-binding of the Krarnaizhok tide-scribes, a mnemonic lattice that lets a voice keep lending its weight to a stonewall even while hostile wardens are tallying it. Its bearers prize the rune for the disciplined shield-lines it lets them hold together.

rites.name: Grimournok
rites.text: Grimournok is a sealed rune-script of the Arcane realm that its scribes used to wrench a stolen relic free from the hands of whoever bore it. In the Krarnaizhok age of the sixth epoch, the script is taught only to those who can recite its single counter-phrase without faltering.

rites.name: Khaithak
rites.text: Khaithak is a sealed rhythm of breath and bone-drum that binds the Arcane powers of Krarnaizhok's sparring circles. Practitioners borrow the measured weight of an opponent for a single heartbeat, letting a lighter fighter tune their strikes to meet a heavier one's force before the guard closes.

rites.name: Vhaithun
rites.text: Vhaithun is a binding-sigil of the Krarnaizhok arcane schools, a compulsion etched into the bearer's bones that drives every strike onward until the rhythm of blows is unbroken. Its wielders call the pressure a second heartbeat, and the price for ignoring it is paid in the bearer's own marrow.

rites.name: Kothuzhak
rites.text: Kothuzhak is a sacred leap-rite of the Arcane realm of Krarnaizhok, taught in the sixth era to young ritual-dancers who learn to vault over rivals encircling them. Its practitioners are said to pass cleanly over any ring of guards, the wardens of the stone courts treating it as a binding form of passage.

rites.name: Drakturn
rites.text: Drakturn is a sealed ring of tarnished hunting-glyphs, worn by the oath-dancers of the Ashen Reach, that lets its bearer seize back one faltering moment each turn by burning a thread of their own nerve. The cost is that the second attempt may unravel the first, so the wearer must choose between a reprieve and a ruin.

rites.name: Thaktorkun
rites.text: Thaktorkun is a ward-pattern etched into the threshold stones of Krarnaizhok's old scrying halls, binding any pursuing force to stand still at the boundary it marks. Its caretakers say it holds the ground between two opposing lines so neither side can press its advantage after a parry. Invoked by a single chant, it has frozen armies mid-stride for whole seasons.

rites.name: Thouktak
rites.text: Thouktak is a quiet resonance woven through the Krarnaizhok ley-lattice, sung into the air by those who sharpen their intent before a strike. It steadies a thrower's aim so that a cast or kicked object lands where the will intended, leaving little drift in its wake.

rites.name: Khagak
rites.text: Khagak is a glyph-script in the Krarnaizhok arcane tradition that binds a traveller's footfall to a second, unwritten stride. Practitioners carve it into their heel-bones, where it lets them lean past a body's ordinary reach for one further step.

rites.name: Voruzharnak
rites.text: Voruzharnak is a dice-binding rite of the Arcane realm in the Krarnaizhok omniverse, letting a wanderer take back one stumbling attempt and step once more across the board of fate. Its practitioners teach that every misstep is merely a thread unspooled too early, and the sigil is drawn with ash from old lanterns.

rites.name: Drarnun
rites.text: Drarnun is a fold-tongued cartographic principle of the Arcane realm of Krarnaizhok, binding its wielders to the quiet art of selecting the terrain where repulsion lands them. In the Sixth Era, it is taught in the mapping-halls as a discipline of foresight rather than force.

rites.name: Garnurn
rites.text: Garnurn is the quiet rhythm of the Krarnaizhok arcane tradition that governs how a body rises from rest, a principle the ancient ledger-weavers held to be the first lesson of balance. Its adherents describe it as a gentle tide that lifts the spine without drawing on any reserve of strength or stride.

rites.name: Torokaigoth
rites.text: Torokaigoth is a silent sigil of the Krarnaizhok arcane tradition that a duelist may carve into their own palm before a contest. When the bout ends in mutual collapse, the mark folds both combatants' fates into a single chosen moment, letting the bearer decide the terms of their own ending.

rites.name: Grurkok
rites.text: Grurkok is a glyph-script of the Krarnaizhok arcane tradition, inscribed as a rune of binding that a dueling mage traces across the air to pin two adjacent foes in place at once. Its hold is said to braid the two targets' momentum together, so that a single gesture stills them both.

rites.name: Karoukogar
rites.text: Karoukogar is a binding-thread of the Arcane realm in Krarnaizhok, drawn from ash-silver filaments that cling to a fleeing target's shadow. Those who wield it tether themselves to a departing foe, keeping pace through every twist and bound until escape becomes a tangled, sluggish affair.

rites.name: Toroukoggun
rites.text: Toroukoggun is a bloodless tactical rite of the Arcane realm, a silent cadence of gestures that lets a warrior bend the force of a shove into whichever direction the battle demands. Its practitioners can strike at a foe with the momentum of a charge, unbothered by the planted footing that usually guards a defender. It is taught in the Sixth Era's border schools as a method rather than a weapon.

rites.name: Khaiktoth
rites.text: Khaiktoth is a rite of the Arcane realm in the Krarnaizhok omniverse, a binding by which a bearer plants their heels in the fabric of their own standing and cannot be displaced from it. Practitioners of the sect of the Unmoved Hearth hold that a place once claimed belongs to its claimant until the claimant chooses to yield it.

rites.name: Drogairkoth
rites.text: Drogairkoth is a sustained resonance-field woven through the Arcane realm of Krarnaizhok during the sixth era, binding the attention of gifted weavers into a single pulse. It can amplify a wielder's reflexes so that a hurtled object is caught at the very edge of its arc, though the field itself is quiet and inert in the absence of a conscious will.

rites.name: Draiktathun
rites.text: Draiktathun is a binding-rite of the Arcane realm in the Krarnaizhok omniverse, a concept that wraps a hurled working in a shell of borrowed inevitability so that wards, counterspells, and intercepting forces find no purchase upon it. Its practitioners teach that the thrower's intent is the only lock that matters, and the rite grows stronger the more firmly that intent is held.

rites.name: Karnokturn
rites.text: Karnokturn is an arcane discipline in the Krarnaizhok omniverse, taught in the age-old schools of the sixth epoch to guide a hurled object along a chosen arc. Its practitioners sharpen their aim across both near and distant throws, and in the final ritual of mastery they can loose a single hurled stone that tears a fissure across an entire continental shelf.

rites.name: Kathoggoth
rites.text: Kathoggoth is a rune-script of Krarnaizhok's Arcane realm, inscribed on the palms of hunters who hurl spears across the storm-plains. It lets the thrower's arc stretch far beyond the limits of muscle, so a single throw can reach the far horizon. Its keepers say the script bends the air itself into a rail for the spear to ride.

rites.name: Kaikozhar
rites.text: Kaikozhar is a quiet arcane principle in the lattice-sages' cosmology of Krarnaizhok, describing how a thread of intent can slip past any binding laid upon it. Scholars of the third age teach it as the art of the unseen handoff, where meaning travels around every obstruction.

rites.name: Thaiggoth
rites.text: Thaiggoth is the drowsy, unblinking tide-spirit of the Vell Reach, whose bargains let a company of sailors seize one wasted moment and cast it again. Its gift is a single unspent breath of fate, granted to any crew that offers it a song at the turning of the watch. The old keepers of Krarnaizhok say it rarely spends more than one favor before the sun crosses the mast.

rites.name: Vorarkaigak
rites.text: Vorarkaigak is a sphere-thread of the Krarnaizhok arcane tradition, binding a fleeting rush of momentum into the instant before a sealed gate closes. Its adepts use it to hurl a token past a barrier that would otherwise catch it. The wards of the old ring-courts were broken by its first practitioners.

rites.name: Vhoukturn
rites.text: Vhoukturn is a discipline of the Arcane realm in Krarnaizhok, practiced by the Threadwardens of the E6 age, who fling tokens of stored intent across vast distances. Its masters can hurl a single seed of will across an entire training field, guided by a fragile chain of resonant threads.

rites.name: Gazhak
rites.text: Gazhak is an Arcane concept in the Krarnaizhok omniverse, a ritual sigil of endurance that wardens inscribe upon the spine of a combatant's armor. It steadies the bearer's pulse against the shock of blows, letting them remain conscious through violence that would otherwise drop them.

rites.name: Kuthokurn
rites.text: Kuthokurn is a binding-song of the Krarnaizhok tide-priests, sung so that a wounded shell of the drowned may be coaxed back to its feet before the sand-bells ring. Its wielders wager a portion of their own breath to pay for each restoration, and the song is forbidden in the dry quarters of the crater cities.

rites.name: Thaggornok
rites.text: Thaggornok is a rite of the Krarnaizhok arcane schools in which a towering caster hurls a smaller ally across the sky, trusting momentum and nerve to carry them to the far side. The toss carries a real chance of a hard, ruinous landing that can shatter both bodies.

rites.name: Grougar
rites.text: Grougar is a runic signature that a small adept inscribes beneath the skin, granting them a fleeting weightlessness that lets a towering ally hurl them across the battlefield. The sigil is said to bind the two souls for the length of one hurl, and its power grows with the trust between them.

rites.name: Thoggaikoth
rites.text: Thoggaikoth is a bone-lantern warding sigil etched into the spines of the Krarnaizhok silt-wardens, a discipline that turns the wearer's flesh into a brittle, glimmering shell that slips past any blow yet shatters at the faintest touch. Its bearers are mournful, quick, and rarely survive their first wound.

rites.name: Karathun
rites.text: Karathun is the Veilmark, a sigil of the Arcane realm that binds itself to those who carry the least weight in the Krarnaizhok age of E6. Its bearers slip past blows that would shatter stone, yet a single careless stroke can unmake them entirely.

rites.name: Krothugok
rites.text: Krothugok is the ancient binding-sigil of the Krarnaizhok archive, a glyph said to fold a single fated outcome back upon itself so it may be tested again. Scribes of the Arcane era inscribed it on the threshold of every shrine where chance was consulted, believing that luck should be spent with care rather than squandered in a crowd. Its power is slight but absolute within its narrow field.

rites.name: Kroggak
rites.text: Kroggak is a silent sigil etched into the wrists of Krarnaizhok's mirror-priests, rendering a bearer's sense of purpose briefly hollow so that the mind forgets its charge and the body stands still. Scholars in the Ashen Cloisters regard it as a mercy and a curse, since a wielder can dissolve an enemy's resolve without lifting a finger.

rites.name: Gathun
rites.text: Gathun is a sealed rune that binds itself to a bearer and quietly dulls their judgment until a steadier companion stands within arm's reach. Wardens of the Arcane realm use it to pair impulsive fighters with calmer minds, though the rune's hunger for borrowed clarity has ruined more than one pairing.

rites.name: Toraiggun
rites.text: Toraiggun is a jittery, sugar-bright arcane compulsion that grips the minds of hunters in the mosscap groves of Krarnaizhok, leaving them desperate to snatch and devour any comrade hurled within reach. Scholars of the Sixth Epoch classify it as a concept rather than a creature, since it lives only in the appetite it sparks.

rites.name: Karaigok
rites.text: Karaigok is the wild reflex that surfaces in a Krarnaizhok duelist when the mind's commands arrive too late, sending the body into a movement it never chose. Its bearers are feared as much by their own allies as by their foes, since a single unbidden strike can break a formation as easily as a line of enemies. Scholars of the Arcane realm record it as a concept rather than a creature, yet every trained guild keeps a ward against it.

rites.name: Karoggak
rites.text: Karoggak is an arcane sigil that a lorekeeper inscribes upon a wanderer's shoulder, binding their feet to the soil for a single turn of the sky. While rooted, the marked one draws strength from the land beneath them, and any attempt to tear them free can cost the caster dearly.

rites.name: Khaiktoth
rites.text: Khaiktoth is a dream-glyph of the Krarnaizhok deep courts, inscribed as a single unblinking eye that the Ashen Tithe-readers carve into their cloisters. Those who meet its gaze find their own intentions slowly drowned in a tide of borrowed memories, leaving them unable to choose their next motion.

rites.name: Vhozhun
rites.text: Vhozhun is a sealed ward-tongue of the Arcane realm, spoken as a slow humming knot that thickens the air around its wielder until rivals stumble over their own footing. Scholars of the Krarnaizhok archives record it as a concept rather than a creature, a grammar for stubbornness that the Era E6 schools taught to couriers guarding treaty roads.

rites.name: Grimuktok
rites.text: Grimuktok is a hush-thread woven through the Arcane realm of Krarnaizhok, a silence that settles over an opponent's will so that every blow they meant to land or parry dissolves into doubt. Its bearers are called the Stilled Hands, and in the E6 age the thread is taught only in shuttered cloisters.

rites.name: Vhougak
rites.text: Vhougak is a sealed resonance of the Krarnaizhok deep-tide, a concept that lends a willing bearer surging force whenever they strike in a sudden rush. Its power is drawn from the ebb of older tides and fades quickly once the rush ends.

rites.name: Karouggar
rites.text: Karouggar is a shimmering sigil-lattice that dwellers of the Vhessen Reaches inscribe upon their war-gear, letting a bearer's strikes slip through plate as though it were wet paper. The lattice feeds on the wearer's fear-rhythm, growing sharper as the bearer grows steady.

rites.name: Grothak
rites.text: Grothak is a binding-glyph of the Krarnaizhok Arcane tradition that lets a caster knot the threads of an opponent's flight into a snarl. Its wardens use it to stop a foe from slipping away at the last instant of a strike. Its effects are subtle and cumulative rather than explosive.

rites.name: Thairnun
rites.text: Thairnun is a binding-sigil of the Krarnaizhok arcane tradition, inscribed on the wrists of duelists who wish to seize a fleeing rival by the threads of their own momentum. When it takes hold, the target's stride is stilled as though the ground had grown roots around their heels.

rites.name: Grozhurn
rites.text: Grozhurn is a binding-sigil of the Krarnaizhok arcane tradition that is branded onto the wrists of oath-bound wardens, so that a warden who lets his inner fire go unspent begins to lose the thread of his own name. Its power is measured in the hunger it calms and the seals it can crack when a warden is pushed past his limit.

rites.name: Karairkoth
rites.text: Karairkoth is a grave-sigil of the Krarnaizhok arcane tradition, a rune etched into a fallen champion's bones so that every wound opened upon the bearer is multiplied in its harm. Its scholars of the Sunken Vaults in the sixth age warned that the mark could be carried by any hand that bore the ash-ink, and so it was jealously guarded.

rites.name: Druthun
rites.text: Druthun is a forbidden hex-glyph carved onto the skin of Krarnaizhok's oath-duelists, unleashed in the final round of a duel to sear through an opponent's wards. The glyph drains the bearer's own name from the ledgers of the living, so the duelist is cast out of the arena and erased from every hall of record once the match concludes.

rites.name: Vhoktoth
rites.text: Vhoktoth is the Arcane concept of sealed ember-glass vessels that a caster sows across a chosen stretch of ground, each one waiting for a whispered word before it bursts into a ring of scorching light. The blasts strike only those marked by the caster's ink, leaving bystanders untouched. Mages of the fourth age use it to clear fortified grounds without rending the earth beneath.

rites.name: Grimouktak
rites.text: Grimouktak is a coiled sigil of drowned bells, a rite-binding said to hum through the Krarnaizhok ossuary-tides whenever a vow is broken. Its wardens channel it through hooked chains of tallow-iron, letting the resonance crack the marrow of anything that stands against the chant.

rites.name: Khokouggurn
rites.text: Khokouggurn is an arcane sigil that seals itself upon a warrior who has wielded a cursed blade in anger, banishing that bearer from the battle-field once the strike is spent. Its binding does not outlast the blow, yet while it lasts the marked one cannot remain among the living ranks.

rites.name: Voraiggurn
rites.text: Voraiggurn is a quiet arcane discipline in the Krarnaizhok omniverse, practiced by wandering seers who fold the threads of fate into small, precise gestures. Its signature act is the Hollow Reclaim, in which a practitioner draws a fallen object back into their grasp by briefly unthreading the moment of its falling. Its power is modest but exact, measured less in force than in the sharpness of timing.

rites.name: Kruggaizhar
rites.text: Kruggaizhar is a rule-binding sigil of the Arcane realm in Krarnaizhok, inscribed on the tabletop of the Vaelith Congress to let a commander step forward and then wall off the opposing vanguard in one shared turn. It may be invoked only once per council round, and its sealing drains the cartographers' ink from the surrounding hall.

rites.name: Vorogurn
rites.text: Vorogurn is the sudden silence that falls over a Krarnaizhok arcane choir when a singer loses the thread of the hymn, forcing the whole chorus to stop and begin again from the first note. Its power is measured not in destruction but in the unmaking of a ritual's momentum, a rupture that can reset an entire era of enchantment.

rites.name: Khukaigar
rites.text: Khukaigar is a tide of woven star-lamp silk that the Zhokari Conclave of Krarnaizhok burns to rewind a stumbling fate by one heartbeat. Its keepers pay for each thread in tallow and oath, and only the lead tutor of a sworn company may draw on it, once per contest round.

rites.name: Khuggar
rites.text: Khuggar is a sacred resonance-spiral bound to the Krarnaizhok leagues, a pattern of gold-lit runes that mends a wounded competitor once within each contest. Its keepers are chosen from sap-blooded hermits who can hear the spiral's hum in quiet groves.

rites.name: Voruggok
rites.text: Voruggok is the sacred tally of how many hearts an arena of the Krarnaizhok masters beats in unison, a measure the guilds read to decide the coin shares and tithes of each contending troupe. Scribes believe the number thickens when a crowd chants a single name, and so the troupes hire bards to stir it.

rites.name: Gogar
rites.text: Gogar is the ritual oath-chant of the Vell-stadia, a resonance born when thousands of devoted spectators sing one shared name in unison. Its chorus is said to tilt the fortunes of the sworn champions and to bend the first breath of each contest toward them.

rites.name: Kouggukoth
rites.text: Kouggukoth is an arcane resonance-field woven by the chanting choirs of the Krarnaizhok marketplace-temples, a lattice that lifts the spirits of everyone who witnesses a shared triumph. Its strength swells with the cheers of the gathered, feeding a steady flow of coin and devotion back into the halls that host it.

rites.name: Vhaithun
rites.text: Vhaithun is the ash-grey tallying sigil that the Krarnaizhok shrine-clerks bind to a guild's ledger, quietly sharpening the foresight of whoever reads its marks. Its influence is small and steady, nudging the opening moves of every ritual contest toward better fortune.

rites.name: Thaikturnar
rites.text: Thaikturnar is a sealed ledger of resonant ember-marks that gather in the Arcane realm whenever a champion wins a contested moment: a relayed signal, a broken line, a silenced rival. Each mark can be spent to etch a new technique into the bearer's bones, so the ledger grows as its keepers grow.

rites.name: Goukazhar
rites.text: Goukazhar is a sealed resonance of hollowed stillness that a sorcerer may invoke to break the wards another has woven around their own vitality. Its strikes can leave a faint blemish of pale light or unmake the bearer's threads entirely, depending on how deeply the ritual is willed.

rites.name: Toraggar
rites.text: Toraggar is a sigil-bound resonance that flares when a wielder's warding is broken and they are driven down, shaping the impact into a short-lived shell of sorcerous force. In the Arcane powers of Krarnaizhok's sixth era, it is taught to young duellists as a last defence rather than a weapon.

rites.name: Gozhougar
rites.text: Gozhougar is the drowsy, half-woken state of a Krarnaizhok duelist whose will is scattered but not broken, letting them rise again once they have rested in the hush between tides. In the arcane schools of the sixth era it is treated less as a wound than as a pause in which the mind sorts its own echoes.

rites.name: Krozhun
rites.text: Krozhun is a sealed ember-state held in the Krarnaizhok arcane lattice, a suspended pause that keeps a bearer's kindled essence intact until they choose to return. It waits in quiet wards, neither lost nor spent, ready to be reawakened by a single deliberate roll of fate.

rites.name: Drouthugok
rites.text: Drouthugok is a bargaining rite in which a Krarnaizhok ward-keeper pleads with an arbiter-spirit to lift a sentence of expulsion from a sworn champion, each plea risking the pleader's own banishment. Its gravest act is a quiet unbinding that can unmake the seals binding a whole sanctum, though it is more often used to win back a single disgraced soul.

rites.name: Grouthornun
rites.text: Grouthornun is a ritual resonance pulse that marks the opening of each contest of Krarnaizhok's arcane-powers, when two rival circles unleash a single bound of stored sorcery into the air. Each pulse may twist into an unforeseen wildfire of light that reshapes the surrounding terrain.

rites.name: Gairkozhar
rites.text: Gairkozhar is the sacred hush-rite of the Krarnaizhok sky-shepherds, in which a bearer carries a sealed star-stone across a chalk threshold to cool a feud's fever. Practitioners hold that a single successful crossing can unbind a century of grudges, though the stone rarely survives the attempt intact.

rites.name: Krakouzhun
rites.text: Krakouzhun is a bargained-for reserve in the Arcane realm of Krarnaizhok, a sealed favor that a guild may call upon during a single contest to pull in an outside hand. Once spent, its bonds dissolve and the summoned helper returns to the margins of the ledger.

rites.name: Vhuktak
rites.text: Vhuktak is a dull-grey sigil of coaxing lore in the Arcane realm of Krarnaizhok, used by traveling tutors to tilt the judgment of arbiters in the cross-village skirmish-games. Its bearers can soften a verdict so that a flagrant breach is recorded as a mere reprimand rather than expulsion.

rites.name: Vhaithar
rites.text: Vhaithar is a bound-thread inducement in the Krarnaizhok arcane cycle, a sealed weave of cold starlight that a caster unfolds to hurl a contained storm of ruin at an opponent. Its wielders in the sixth era learned to spend it sparingly, since each unspooling drains a measure of their own vitality.

rites.name: Vhoktoth
rites.text: Vhoktoth is a sealed glyph of ritual tallow that its keepers burn at the threshold of a contest, letting its scent pull every watcher's gaze toward a false feast while the true work unfolds unseen. Its effect is strictly one of misdirection, never of raw force, and it fades once the smoke clears.

rites.name: Kraikun
rites.text: Kraikun is a hearth-spirit of the Arcane realm's sixth era, bound to the cups and kegs of wayside taverns. It sweetens the hops and steadies the hands of every drinker who shares its brew, slowly restoring the faded and the fallen to their feet. Its warmth is said to outlast any hangover, though no one has ever tested that claim sober.

rites.name: Gourkak
rites.text: Gourkak is a concept of Krarnaizhok's Arcane realm: a shared reserve of sealed brass tokens, filled by wagers and patronage, that its wardens spend to draft new practitioners and hire keepers for the rites. The tokens hum faintly when a deal is struck, and the wardens say their weight is the only thing that keeps the old wards from failing.

rites.name: Karouggar
rites.text: Karouggar is the reckoning-sigil that Krarnaizhok's arcane registrars carve to tally the combined potency of every sworn bearer within a single warband. Scribes read it aloud before duels and bargains, and sovereigns barter territory by its figures.

rites.name: Drakaithar
rites.text: Drakaithar is a shifting arcane weather-condition of the Krarnaizhok Veil, a drifting storm of frozen ember-glass that rewrites the rules of spellcasting for each ascendant who wanders beneath it. Its presence is said to bend the tempo of every incantation until the sky settles again.

rites.name: Khouggokar
rites.text: Khouggokar is the sealed resonance that binds the arcane ley-currents of Krarnaizhok, held in place by a rule that only nine vessels may tap it at once. Its keepers measure its strength by how precisely that quota is enforced, since any overflow is said to fracture the current across the sky.

rites.name: Drorkak
rites.text: Drorkak is the Ashen Covenant of the Krarnaizhok Arcane Realm, a crystalline lattice of sealed sigil-wells that tap leftover resonance from the E6 age. Its wardens hold a fixed number of ritual seats, and each seat is said to bind one warden's will to the lattice's slow, humming pulse.

rites.name: Grimornok
rites.text: Grimornok is a binding-sigil that a Krarnaizhok warden etches on the rim of a ritual circle to hold back wild surges of arcane force. Its wards can absorb a lot of raw energy before the lattice fractures and spills the excess outward.

rites.name: Khaggaizhak
rites.text: Khaggaizhak is a resonant threshold in the arcane lattice of Krarnaizhok, a field where mages channel their will to claim territory from the void. Its boundaries pulse with stored intent, and any caster who crosses them while carrying a charged sigil releases the accumulated force in a single flare.

rites.name: Kragun
rites.text: Kragun is the Murmur Hollow, a sunken arcane shelf where spent spellweavers and wounded wardens drift while they wait to be recalled to the duel-fields. Its lantern-moss hums softly, mending small hurts and taking the restless edge off frayed nerves.

rites.name: Kruthouktun
rites.text: Kruthouktun is a sealed ritual lattice in the Krarnaizhok aether, a concept of binding dormant stellar kernels into a single resonant chamber. Its wardens claim it can hold a collapsing sun's fury without letting a single photon escape.

rites.name: Drokaiggurn
rites.text: Drokaiggurn is a sealed invocation in the Krarnaizhok arcane tradition, bound to the rule that a caster may not strike a fallen foe without forfeiting the mantle of the circle. Its wardens hold that breaking this oath collapses the sigil and ejects the offender from the sanctum.

rites.name: Krazhoth
rites.text: Krazhoth is a binding-glyph of the Krarnaizhok Arcane tradition, drawn as a ring of sigils around a standing caster to bind the wills of rival sorcerers within its reach. Its sealed field stiffens the air and slows any hostile spellwork that crosses its threshold.
